FF Kashem Fakir now fights for a morsel of bread
2014-12-19T00:00:53+06:00 | S Dilip Roy, Lalmonirhat
https://www.thedailystar.net/ff-kashem-fakir-now-fights-for-a-morsel-of-bread-56032

A valiant freedom fighter in Sadar upazila now runs his family of five by selling medicines for rat killing. The lone bread earner, FF Abul Kashem Fakir, 64, is facing great trouble to support his family as his earnings have drastically fell. “Days were when I earned Tk 150 to 200 a day by selling medicines for killing rat, louse and scabies at my makeshift shop at markets in the district. But my earnings have dropped alarmingly nowadays,” said Abul Kashem. Altaf Hossain, a resident of Alorupa intersection area in the district town, said although Kashem's medicines are very effective, many now do not buy them for fear of fake medicines. Kashem, son of late Ahmed Fakir of Adampur village under Moksedpur upazila in Gopalganj district, fought against Pakistani occupation forces under Sector 8 during the country's Liberation War in 1971. After the country was freed, he shifted to Lalmonirhat town and married Fatema Begum of Shaheed Shahjahan Colony in Sadar upazila. His two sons--Abu Kawsar, 24, and Abu Sayeed, 15-- work as hawkers in the town while his daughter Amena Khatun, 19, studied BA at a local college. “Although I get freedom fighters' monthly allowance, it is too an small amount for me to maintain the family. I face acute trouble when I can't bear the education cost of my daughter,” said the valiant freedom fighter.
